A reusable JWT check

Source: R/jwt.R
jwt_decoder.Rd

jwt_decoder() fixes the key and every check of jwt_decode() once, and returns a function of the token that applies them. Use it where the same policy guards many requests.

Usage

jwt_decoder(
  key,
  algorithms,
  audience = NULL,
  issuer = NULL,
  subject = NULL,
  type = "JWT",
  required = "exp",
  claims = list(),
  validate = NULL,
  max_age = NULL,
  leeway = 60,
  decrypt = NULL,
  limits = jose_limits()
)

Arguments

key

A jwk, a jwk_set, or a function of the header returning one.

algorithms

The signature algorithms to accept, such as "HS256".

audience

The audiences this caller accepts, or NULL.

issuer

The issuer this caller accepts, or NULL.

subject

The subject this caller accepts, or NULL.

type

The expected typ, or NULL to skip the check.

required

Names of claims that must be present.

claims

Further expectations, as a list of values or functions with unique names.

validate

A function of the claims list that must return TRUE, or NULL.

max_age

The greatest age, in seconds, of iat, or NULL.

leeway

Seconds of clock skew to allow.

decrypt

For a JWT sent as a JWE, the key and algorithms to decrypt it, from jwe_decryption(); NULL refuses a JWE.

limits

Resource limits, from jose_limits().

Value

A function function(token, now = Sys.time()) returning the claims, as jwt_decode() does.

Examples

key <- jwk_oct(as.raw(1:32))
check <- jwt_decoder(key, "HS256", audience = "api", issuer = "me")
jwt <- jwt_encode(
  list(iss = "me", aud = "api"),
  key,
  "HS256",
  expires_in = 60
)
check(jwt)$iss
#> [1] "me"
